title: Any other holder may re-queue an escalated item: resolve opens to holders over a new edge

story.as_a: a holder session, or loopctl's own sweep
story.i_want_to: send an item another holder escalated back to the queue
story.so_that: an escalation means 'needs a different holder' and never waits for Mark

rationale: PRD R4 and section 4: 'escalated' stops meaning 'parked for a human'. Today POST /stories/:id/stage/resolve is role: :user (story_escalation_controller.ex:43) and every edge out of escalated is :human_resolution (stage_machine.ex:211), which Stages.human?/1 (stages.ex:2145) grants only to a :user key no dispatch minted, so every escalation waits for Mark. Only the role split between escalate (:agent) and resolve (:user) stops a session resolving its own escalation; no check compares the two principals. This story adds one holder edge, escalated -> queued, and the self_resolve_blocked guard, and leaves the :human_resolution edges exactly as they are, because Gate A, the :review_missing hold, escalated -> done and spec validation read them as 'a human decided'.

acceptance_criteria.description: StageMachine.transitions/0 gains {:escalated, :queued, :holder_resolution}; StageMachine.clears(:escalated, :queued, :holder_resolution) equals clears(:escalated, :queued, :human_resolution); every {:escalated, to, :human_resolution} edge and human_only?/1 are unchanged.
Spec.allowed_transitions/1 excludes {:escalated, :queued, :holder_resolution} for :judge, :draft and :build, and Spec compilation refuses a spec naming it with a message naming the edge.

The resolve route's plug is role: :agent (RequireHumanAnchor kept). Escalations.resolve/3 takes :human_resolution for a caller Stages.human?/1 accepts, for all four targets as today; for any other caller it takes :holder_resolution when to is queued and returns {:error, :human_required} (422) for detected, done or failed, changing nothing.

A non-human caller is refused before any claim release, changing nothing (claim, epoch, session dispatch and stage row): 409 self_resolve_blocked when its api key's holder_id equals the actor_holder_id of the event that moved the item into escalated (an escalation event with no actor_holder_id blocks no holder), and 409 holder_required when its key carries no holder_id and it is not loopctl's sweep actor.

A holder resolution of an item that entered escalated over :review_missing is refused 409 review_missing_unreviewed, changing nothing, unless ReviewCustody.reviewed_revision?/4 holds for the item's landed revision; a human resolution of the same item is unaffected.

After a holder resolution, GateAInput.for_story/2 resolves the item's Gate A input from its persisted triage (:persisted_triage or :missing), never :human_resolution, so the merge gate judges Gate A again.

MCP resolve_escalation accepts the agent key (holder credential) as well as the user key, and its description names the holder edge (to: queued only), self_resolve_blocked, holder_required, review_missing_unreviewed and human_required for the other targets.

On the chg route, a landed event whose landed diff touches an independent path leaves the item merged only when MergePrecondition.independent_verification/2 (US-52.12) is :ok for the landed revision; otherwise, or when the diff cannot be read, the item is escalated over the new control-only reason :independent_unverified, held as a :review_missing hold is, and leaves over the holder edge only once the fact is :ok.

test_cases.name: the holder edge exists and clears what a human re-queue clears (unit)
expected_results: true; equal lists; four human edges, human_only?(:holder_resolution) false

test_cases.name: no spec may name the holder edge (unit)
preconditions: a :judge spec module literal naming {:escalated, :queued, :holder_resolution} in outcomes
expected_results: compile error naming :holder_resolution; edge absent from all three lists

test_cases.name: edge chosen by caller; holder limited to queued (DataCase + ConnCase)
preconditions: an item escalated over :session_escalated by holder A (release 3 holder fixtures); holder B's agent key; a user key no dispatch minted
steps: POST /stage/resolve to: done with B's key
POST to: queued with B's key
on a second escalated item, POST to: done with the user key
expected_results: 422 human_required and nothing changed; 200 and the event edge holder_resolution; 200 over human_resolution

test_cases.name: the escalating holder cannot resolve, and nothing is destroyed (DataCase)
preconditions: holder A escalated the item under its session dispatch; an item escalated over :attempts_exhausted by control
steps: re-read story claim_epoch, assigned_holder_id, dispatch revoked_at, stage
resolve the control-escalated item with A's holder_id
expected_results: {:error, :self_resolve_blocked}; all unchanged; the control-escalated item resolves

test_cases.name: a key with no holder is refused (ConnCase)
preconditions: an orchestrator key with no holder_id; an escalated item

test_cases.name: a review_missing hold leaves over the holder edge only once reviewed (DataCase)
preconditions: a chg story escalated over :review_missing (fixtures from test/loopctl/changes/review_custody_test.exs); holder B
steps: insert a review_records row with reviewer_dispatch_id for the landed sha

test_cases.name: Gate A is not cleared by a holder re-queue (DataCase)
preconditions: an item escalated over :triage_escalate with a bound triage dispatch whose verdict is escalate
steps: resolve as holder B to queued

test_cases.name: two holders resolving at once: one wins, the other is told the stage (DataCase, two connections)
preconditions: an escalated item; holders B and C; Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology for two connections
steps: resolve as B and as C concurrently
expected_results: one {:ok, row}; the other {:error, {:not_escalated, :queued}}; one holder_resolution event

test_cases.name: resolve_escalation sends with the agent key and documents the refusals (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server with only LOOPCTL_AGENT_KEY set; a stub apiCall
expected_results: POST sent with the agent key; description contains self_resolve_blocked and holder_required

test_cases.name: a chg landing on an independent path holds until verified (DataCase, chg fixtures, PullRequestSourceMock)
preconditions: a chg story with a recorded review (fixtures from test/loopctl/changes/review_custody_test.exs); triggers with independent_paths lib/gate/**; the mock compare for the landed sha lists lib/gate/a.ex
steps: apply its landed event with no independent verifier
record verification by a separated verifier on another runner with e2e green, then resolve as holder B
apply a twin's landed event with the compare read failing
expected_results: escalated over :independent_unverified; queued then on through verify, not refused; escalated over :independent_unverified

technical_notes: Edges: @human_resolution at lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_machine.ex:211; add the holder edge to @transitions (:286) and a clears/3 clause beside :947. chained?/3 (:865) already chains every edge from escalated, so the holder edge writes a chain entry ('story_stage_escalation_resolved', stages.ex:2371).
Spec: Spec.allowed_transitions/1 (lib/loopctl/agents/spec.ex:355-363) and check_archetype_transitions/1 (:651); add a StageMachine.holder_resolution_edges/0 and exclude it beside human_only?/1.

Resolve: Escalations.resolve/3 (lib/loopctl/delivery/escalations.ex:417) builds transition {:escalated, to, :human_resolution} at :419; choose the edge from Stages.human?/1 (stages.ex:2145, make it public as Stages.human_principal?/1) BEFORE Stages.precheck/2, and run the self, holder and review_missing checks in the same pre-release block, so the #862 rule (a refused resolve destroys nothing) holds for every new refusal.

Who escalated: the newest 'transitioned' event into escalated carries actor_holder_id (provided by release 3, README names table: work-item event log); the same newest-event read ReviewCustody.review_missing_escalated?/3 uses (lib/loopctl/changes/review_custody.ex:303). The caller's holder_id is on its api_keys row (release 3, README names table: holder credential).

Controller: plug at lib/loopctl_web/controllers/story_escalation_controller.ex:43 becomes role: :agent; pass holder_id from conn.assigns.current_api_key; add 409 self_resolve_blocked, holder_required, review_missing_unreviewed to the resolve operation (:192-197) and rewrite its description and the moduledoc lines that say only a human resolves (:3-16, :39-42).

review_missing: ReviewCustody.reviewed_revision?/4 (review_custody.ex:245) with the landed revision ensure_landed_review/3 (:272) computes; ensure_landed_review/3 itself is unchanged and still gates verify.
Gate A: GateAInput (lib/loopctl/delivery/gate_a_input.ex:15-21) matches the stored edge string 'human_resolution'; no change, only the test.
The sweep actor that AC-52.31.4 admits is defined by US-52.34; this story accepts actor_label 'worker:escalation_sweep' with an attested [] lineage only from in-process callers, never from a key.
MCP: resolveEscalation in mcp-server/lib/delivery-loop.js:245 drops its user-key-only guard and uses the agent key when no user key is set; declaration at mcp-server/index.js:9272.
Docs: docs/agent-delivery-loop.md:24 and :193 say escalated is parked for a human and resolve needs a user key; rewrite both. CHANGELOG.md: the resolve route's role and its new 409s.

chg route: the landed effect is EventEffects.after_move/5 for 'landed' (lib/loopctl/changes/event_effects.ex:564), where the :review_missing hold is taken through escalate_raw/5. The landed diff is a forge read (PullRequestSource.compare/3, pull_request_source.ex:384), so it is never made inside the event transaction: the landed effect enqueues Loopctl.Workers.ChgIndependentPathsWorker (unique per story and merge_sha) in that transaction, and the job reads the diff, runs Gate B with the repo's independent_paths, and escalates under the story lock when the fact is not :ok. :independent_unverified joins @release_escalations-style control-only reasons in stage_machine.ex and the holder edge refuses to release it until independent_verification/2 (US-52.12) is :ok, in the same pre-release block as the review_missing check (AC-52.31.5).
non_goals: Re-triage, cancel and close by a holder: US-52.32.
The sweep that re-queues escalated items on its own: US-52.34.
Changing any :human_resolution edge or the escalate route's exact_role: :agent gate.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: one request against loopctl's own Postgres; a client that loses the answer retries and AC-52.31.3's compare-and-set answers not_escalated naming the new stage.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.31.4: who escalated is read from the append-only event log, never from session-supplied text, so a restart cannot change who may resolve.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.31.3: the transition is a compare-and-set on escalated, so a retried resolve finds the item queued and is refused not_escalated; TC-52.31.8 shows two concurrent resolves write one event. AC-52.31.8's job is unique per story and merge_sha.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.31.8: the chg landed diff is read by a job outside the event transaction, so a slow forge never holds chg's event apply; the resolve itself makes no network call, and a busy lock answers 503 within Capacity.lock_timeout_ms as today.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the request process.

definition_of_done: On production, an item escalated by one session is re-queued by a second session's resolve_escalation(to: queued) and its timeline shows edge holder_resolution with the second holder as actor.
SELECT count(*) FROM story_stage_events WHERE edge = 'holder_resolution' AND actor_holder_id = (the escalating event's actor_holder_id) returns 0.
defaults: A control escalation (no actor_holder_id) may be re-queued by any holder.
A key with no holder_id that is not a human is refused (holder_required) rather than compared by agent_id, because every fleet session shares one agent_id.
